chris_infra: Heads-up — over the last 10m we're seeing sustained Pending pods in us-west1-s (gpu node pools). Cluster autoscaler can't get new GPUs because cloud reports zone-level quota exhaustion in 3 zones. Proposing a temporary cross-cluster redispatch to us-west2 nodes to avoid customer-facing throttles. Thoughts? :thinking:

devops-bot: ALERT: [GPU_QUOTA_EXHAUSTION] us-west1 - PendingPods=67, EvictedPods=4, NodePoolsAtCapacity=[gpu-pool-1,gpu-pool-2] (detected at 2034567885)

maya_sre: Can we get the pending pod manifest summaries? are these interactive low-latency jobs or batch inference? That affects routing and toleration strategy. Also need to check if us-west2 has matching driver/kernel versions before moving workloads.

chris_infra: Most are short-lived online-serve pods (p95 latency SLO). I've pulled a sample: 48/67 are annotated runType=interactive, priorityClass=high. If we shift them to us-west2 we must preserve node labels and nvidia driver compatibility.

sam_platform: Two immediate constraints: (1) cross-cluster traffic for requests might increase egress (customers in us-west1 -> us-west2) — cost + latency; (2) service discovery: some services use cluster-local ILB endpoints. We can either: a) warp traffic at edge (LB-level regional failover), or b) do pod-level redispatch and keep traffic routed to the same LB but backhauled — latter will cost more.

jordan_cost: Quick sanity on costs: us-west2 on-demand GPUs ~+12% vs us-west1 spot; but running inference there avoids user errors and retries which cost more. We should estimate egress delta first. Also consider spin-up of a reserve warm pool in us-west2 vs redispatching current pods.

maya_sre: Operational playbook draft (short):
1) Create a standby nodepool in us-west2 with label gpu.redispatch=true and same kubelet/drivers.
2) Patch the failing deployments with a redispatch annotation to allow our controller to evict+recreate in target cluster.
3) Use a short-lived priorityClass + PodDisruptionBudget exemption for high-priority traffic.
4) Monitor p95 latency, egress bytes, and failed image pulls.

Example kubectl snippet to label and cordon before creating pool:```bash
# create nodepool in gcloud (example)
gcloud container node-pools create redispatch-standby --cluster=redwood-us-west2 --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g --num-nodes=2 --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1" --labels=gpu.redispatch=true
# add toleration/taint on target pool if needed
```

chris_infra: To add — we built a lightweight controller prototype (RegionalCapacityAgent) that uses the cluster API and a central placement queue. Workflow I'm proposing:
- mark pods with annotation redispatch/allow=true (deployment-level toggle)
- RegionalCapacityAgent watches pending pods and available target pools across regions, then issues a delete on the pod (graceful) with an admission hint so the controller on target cluster creates equivalent Pod with original metadata and a transient affinity to the new nodepool.

Controller patch example (pseudo):```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  annotations:
    redispatch/from-cluster: us-west1
    redispatch/origin-poduid: "..."
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "redispatch"
  nodeSelector:
    gpu.redispatch: "true"
```

alex_ops: How do we rollback if us-west2 experiences drift or networking issues? We need a canary: pick one small customer route, flip annotation, and ensure metrics pipeline (tracing + logs + cost) captures delta. Also ensure IAM service account used by controller has readonly on origin cluster and create on target cluster only.

maya_sre: Agreed. Canary plan: 5 pods first, 30m observation window, auto-rollback if >3% latency regression or >5% error increase. Set a temporary egress budget alarm.

chris_infra: Action items:
- I will spin up standby nodepool in us-west2 (ETA 18m) and run driver verification (chris).
- sam will audit LB routing options and egress impact (ETA 30m).
- maya will prepare the canary playbook and alert thresholds (ETA 20m).
- alex will validate RegionalCapacityAgent SA perms and create RBAC doc (ETA 40m).

Any objections to proceeding now? :thumbsup: / :thumbsdown:

alex_ops: +1 from me, proceed but gate canary with the metric alarms.

jordan_cost: +1 but keep me in the loop for cost projection updates.

sam_platform: I'll post LB routing options in 20m.

chris_infra: Thanks team — starting the standby pool now. Will post driver test logs here when ready.
